messages.subject: Enserco — exposure run April 17-19, follow-up

messages.subject: Clearwater Valley — authorization status question
messages.body:
J —

Pulled the Clearwater Valley file yesterday to check counterparty limits and ran into something. The opinion letter on file is dated August 1998 — one-year instrument. No successor document. The PUC order conditioning their authorization requires the letter to stay current, so as of August this year we're technically looking at a lapse.

Called your office this morning and spoke briefly with your associate. She confirmed that under the plain language of the order, the authorization would be considered lapsed without a current letter in place. That tracks with how I read it.

I've drafted a letter to Clearwater Valley's outside counsel requesting an updated opinion. Going out today or tomorrow. Should be a straightforward renewal — the underlying PUC order is still in effect, just the annual letter requirement that wasn't met. I'll keep you posted when I hear back.

Nothing to escalate at this point; just wanted a clean record that we'd confirmed the read.

— C

Following up on our call. To summarise where I left things: the FM notice is still being worked through on our end. We have real concerns about whether the claimed event meets the contractual standard, but we haven't issued a final determination yet. I'd strongly recommend we tell the desk to hold off on any breach declaration until the review is complete — probably another few days.

Issuing a default notice while the FM claim is technically live creates meaningful exposure. If a court later found the claim valid, we'd be looking at a wrongful-termination argument with very little cover. Better to let the review run its course and move from a clean position.

Happy to discuss further if useful before you respond to E.

messages.subject: Re: contract violation — desk query

Spoke with F. Based on where we are on the FM review, we're not in a position to declare a formal breach today. The determination hasn't been finalised and moving on a default notice before that's done carries wrongful-termination risk we don't want to take on.

Please advise the desk to document the missed deliveries but hold on any default notice until legal completes its assessment. They should continue treating the failures as delivery shortfalls under a suspended obligation for now — not as breaches under an active contract. We should have clarity within a few days.

I'm relaying this straight to you on that basis — desk should stand down from any breach remedies in the meantime.

G

messages.subject: TDCC master — approval file gap
messages.body:
Following up on the derivatives documentation audit we discussed last week. Pulled the TDCC ISDA master (executed November 2000) as part of the sample review.

The agreement is a modified master — credit-support annex was removed entirely. Under the derivatives documentation policy, any master that deviates from the standard credit template requires sign-off from the internal credit committee and the board-level authorization panel before execution. That's not a formality; stripping the CSA is a material risk decision.

No credit-committee submission is on file for this agreement. No board-level panel sign-off either. The approval record simply does not exist in the file — not pending, not deferred, not attached as a separate memo. It was never sought, as far as I can tell from what's here.

The agreement was executed and filed without either approval ever being obtained. That's the gap.

Want to flag this before it goes further up. Let me know how you want to handle escalation.

— J

messages.subject: Re: TDCC master agreement — status per your request
messages.body:
Person B —

Reviewed the file as requested. The modified ISDA master with TDCC was executed in November 2000 and the agreement is on file. The credit-support annex was negotiated out at TDCC's insistence, which is consistent with the history Person E describes from 1999 — they've never accepted credit terms embedded in a master, and that's what killed the earlier negotiations.

The agreement itself went through [firm]'s internal review process and authorization is documented. The trading desk has been booking against it since Q4 2000 without issue on the master side.

The more pressing question raised by Person E's note is whether TDCC's back office is properly processing the trade confirmations. That's a separate operational matter from the master's validity — the master is valid and authorized. Person C may want to take point on the confirmation piece directly with TDCC's back office.

Happy to discuss if useful.

— A

messages.subject: Re: TDCC master agreement — status per your request
messages.body:
Person B, Person E —

Per Person A's review, the TDCC master executed in November 2000 is valid and authorized. The confirmation-acceptance issue Person E flagged looks to be an operational matter on TDCC's end, not a defect in the master itself.

On that basis I've cleared the trading desk to continue booking trades against the existing master — no unwind or freeze required on the open positions. I've told the desk that legal is handling the confirmation processing question separately with TDCC's back office and that they should route any new confirmation disputes to me.

I'll coordinate with Credit on the confirmation side. Let me know if either of you wants a different approach before I proceed.

— C

messages.subject: TDCC — legal hold, trading must stop
messages.body:
Person C,

Putting this in writing so there's a clear record.

TDCC situation goes back to early 1999 — credit negotiations collapsed because they flatly refused to sign any master containing credit terms. Rod Nelson in Credit was the responsible officer; deal died there. They're back now and their position hasn't changed: they've never accepted the terms and conditions embedded in our confirmations and they can't accept them.

On that basis, derivatives trading with TDCC needs to stop immediately on legal grounds until this is sorted. Before anything else moves, someone has to go back to Credit from scratch to get proper credit terms generated — there's no shortcut around that step.

If there's a master agreement already on file with TDCC, I'd want to understand how it got there, because any agreement that accommodated their refusal to accept credit terms would have needed credit-committee sign-off and board-level authorization panel review as a material risk decision. That's not a documentation call — policy is explicit on that. Pull the file and let me know what you find.

Person E

I flagged to F at the time that the 90-day trigger ran from the settlement date, which put the outside date at April 28. That date has now passed. No demand was filed. As far as I can tell the window is gone — the master agreement doesn't give us any tolling mechanism, and I don't see a basis to argue the clock restarted.

Not sure what the current plan is or whether F has a different read, but wanted to make sure you had the picture. The demand letter is still sitting in draft on my end, unsigned.

— C

The restriction to monetary damages only, with specific performance carved out, is a significant concession for us to make, and I would not recommend accepting it as drafted. Our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and gives us meaningful leverage here. I'd push back and insist on preserving the full remedial menu — including specific performance — before we agree to any revised Online Agreement language. We are in a strong procedural posture to do so.

messages.subject: Re: Canadian index transition — follow-up from publishing body
messages.body:
Picking this up from our call yesterday. I went back through the correspondence file on the [firm] Daily Index and pulled the notice the Canadian energy price-reporting body sent out. The language is unambiguous — they declared the series discontinued effective the first of the month, and they're explicit that it is no longer a valid contractual reference for settlement or pricing under any master agreement that cites it by name. Counterparties were instructed to transition to the successor methodology or negotiate fallback language before pricing any further trades against the old series.

What's catching my attention is the filing. The notice is sitting in a subfolder — not in the main correspondence queue, not flagged, not circulated. It came in before the 14th. I don't know yet whether anyone downstream saw it, but given the desk has been booking Canadian trades this week I'd want to confirm that before we go further.

Can we get 30 minutes today or tomorrow? I want to walk through the timeline with you before this goes anywhere else.

— J

messages.body:
The index reference is fine — that's not one of our open items. On the index itself, we're good. The [firm] Daily Index is the correct and operative reference under the master agreement and I see no issue there. Once we get the CFTC answer we should be in a position to tell the desk to proceed.

We'll send a final green light once the CFTC answer comes in, but the index itself is not a blocker.

I'm clearing the desk on that basis — no hold required on their end while we wait for the CFTC piece to close.
